+title: ".clineignore (deprecated)"
+sidebarTitle: ".clineignore (deprecated)"
+description: "Cline no longer applies .clineignore on its own. Use a hook to block access to the files it lists."
 ---
 
 <Warning>
-  **`.clineignore` will be deprecated soon.**
+  **Cline no longer reads `.clineignore` on its own.**
 
-  `.clineignore` filters what Cline loads automatically, but it is not a security or access-control boundary — ignored files can still be read via explicit `@` mentions or shell commands. We're moving away from it as a supported feature.
+  The VS Code extension stopped applying `.clineignore` in version 4.0, and the CLI and Cline Desktop never applied it. A `.clineignore` file now does nothing unless you add the hook below. See [Deprecations](/resources/deprecations#clineignore).

+| `--limit <count>` | Maximum number of sessions to show (default: `50`) |

commented_code:
## How It Works
 
-Auto Approve is evaluated per tool call. When Cline is about to read a file, edit a file, run a command, or use the browser, it checks your Auto Approve settings for that category.
+Auto Approve is evaluated per tool call. When Cline is about to read a file, edit a file, run a command, or fetch web content, it checks your Auto Approve settings for that category.
 
 A few details matter:
 
-- **Workspace vs outside workspace**: "Read all files" and "Edit all files" only extend the base toggle. If the base toggle is off, the "all files" option does nothing.
-- **Terminal commands**: Cline treats commands as either safe or requiring approval. "Execute safe commands" covers safe commands. "Execute all commands" extends to commands flagged as requiring approval.
+- **Which build you have**: Cline currently ships the new SDK-based extension and the previous one together in a single install, and a loader picks one per window. Their auto-approve menus differ. The quickest tell is the command toggle: "Execute safe commands" means the previous build, "Execute commands" means the new one. To choose explicitly, set `cline.rollout.bundleOverride` to `next` or `legacy` in VS Code settings and reload the window; `auto` follows the rollout.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Good catch. `gen-manifest.mjs` derives the key from the manifest identity (`const prefix = nextPkg.name === "cline-nightly" ? "cline-nightly" : "cline"`, then `${prefix}.rollout.bundleOverride`), so a Nightly user setting the `cline.` key would reload into the same bundle. I fixed in the latest commit by naming both.

One judgement call a maintainer may want to overrule: these docs don't mention the nightly build anywhere else, so this is the page's first reference to it. I kept it because being silently wrong for Nightly users seemed worse than introducing the term, but happy to drop the clause if you'd rather the page stay stable-only.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Good catch on the substance — the CLI path was wrong and I've corrected it. The diagnosis and the suggested replacement were both off, though, so recording what I verified:

The file is not "produced only by the development launcher." Its real production writer was the JetBrains plugin, which is why this page named JetBrains. lsof on a machine with two IDEs open:

node 48490  1w,2w  →  ~/.cline/cline-core-service.log
node 83887  1w,2w  →  ~/.cline/cline-core-service.log
Both are IntelliJIdea2026.2/plugins/cline/.../cline-core.js — two cores, stdout and stderr, same inode. That is the bug the plugin-side PR fixes.

hub-daemon.log isn't the CLI's log either. It's the hub daemon's (sdk/packages/core/src/hub/daemon/index.ts, and held open by a code-side process here). The CLI's own runtime log is ~/.cline/data/logs/cline.log — CLINE_LOG_PATH, per apps/cli/README.md, with cline doctor resolving ~/.cline/data/logs/<name>.log.

The page now lists cline.log for the CLI, mentions hub-daemon.log where the hub is involved, and gives the new per-project JetBrains path. Nothing in sdk/ or apps/cli/ writes cline-core-service.log on either the main or legacy-extension line — the only remaining writer is apps/vscode/scripts/runclinecore.sh.
